Amaya is a recent UAlbany alum who served as a hotline assistant with the Middle Earth Peer Assistance Program and supported first-year students' transitions into college through First-Year Experience programming and Writing and Critical Inquiry courses. 
Amaya is currently a Prevention Navigator for Project ACCESS, a prevention service grant aimed at helping minoritized students navigate health and well-being resources on-and off-campus. 
Amaya's academic interests center on trauma informed care and peer-to-peer support.  
In her free time, Amaya enjoys reading, watching movies, and spending time outside. 
Pronouns: she/her/hers, they/them/theirs

NavDescription: Amanda Fowler is a recent graduate of Binghamton University’s Master of Social Work Program. She earned her bachelor’s degree in human development & psychology with a minor in Sociology from University at Albany - SUNY. Amanda is passionate about advocating for and implementing harm reduction resources and strategies on college campuses. She is currently Project Manager for Project ACCESS. In her free time, she loves to play video games, watch football, workout, and spend time with loved ones. Pronouns: she/her/hers
VirtualInfo: Virtual Appointments are on WEDNESDAYS ONLY (Video on is required)

NavDescription: Yaa is a PhD Candidate in the Educational Policy & Leadership doctoral program at UAlbany. She has over 15 years of experience in higher education administration, student counselling, and mentorship. She holds an MS in Educational Policy and Leadership (UAlbany), MPhil in Educational Leadership and Management (Ghana), an MSc in International Business and Corporate Governance (UK), a Post Graduate Diploma in Education (Ghana), and a BA in Psychology and Sociology (Ghana).

I am a second-year master's student in the Educational Psychology and Methodology program at UAlbany. I have a Bachelor's degree in Psychology from Hyderabad, India, and have prior clinical experience as an Assistant speech therapist working with children with developmental and behavioral needs. My professional interests include neuroscience, neuroplasticity, and the intersection of AI and human development. Currently, I am conducting a meta-analysis exploring the relationship between communication and language interventions and children's externalizing behaviors. Outside of academics, I enjoy reading fiction.

LJ is a licensed school counselor with an M.Ed. in school counseling and an M.A. in psychological counseling from Teachers College, Columbia University. Currently, LJ is a third-year Ph.D. student in counseling psychology at S.U.N.Y. Albany and is interested in exploring the interplay between multi-level stigma and different systems of oppression and their intersectional impacts on well-being for individuals with marginalized identities. Through his research, LJ seeks to deepen his understanding of the multifaceted challenges individuals in marginalized communities face and to catalyze culturally relevant adaptations of interventions to better serve marginalized clients.

Tyler is a first-year student in the Master of Science in Licensed Mental Health Counseling program at UAlbany. He previously worked in the biopharmaceutical industry and holds a B.S. from Rochester Institute of Technology and a B.A. in Psychology. His professional interests include substance use disorders, trauma, mental health prevention, Motivational Interviewing, and SBIRT. Outside of his studies, he works as an EMT and enjoys reading, hiking, traveling, riding his motorcycle, and spending time with his dogs and family.

Edward Osterhout is an M.S. Counseling student at the University at Albany. His research interests include gender differences in help‑seeking for mental health care. Edward is a huge foodie and enjoys kayaking and hiking. His background includes equine‑assisted therapy with military veterans and children on the autism spectrum.

I am a current MSW student originally from East New York, Brooklyn, with a Bachelor of Technology in Canine Training & Management. As a queer woman, I strive to build open, comfortable, and inclusive spaces for everyone. I personally trained and certified my cat as a therapy animal, bringing comfort to local libraries, nursing homes, and healthcare facilities through animal-assisted activities.

I am entering my fourth year in UAlbany’s Doctoral School Psychology program. Professionally, I am driven to help others through culturally-responsive prevention and intervention efforts. I am interested in continuing to research crisis response, suicide prevention, and internalizing disorders. I have interned within the elementary and middle school age groups conducting comprehensive psychological evaluations and behavioral assessments, implementing behavior plans, counseling students working through a variety of needs, and analyzing data. I am Therapeutic Crisis Intervention for Schools (TCIS) trained and seek to use this training to assist in de-escalating crises and teach coping skills. Personally, I am interested in crafting, reading, spending time with my friends, being outdoors, finding the best coffee in the Capital Region, and playing with my two cats (Aries and Dunkin).

I am a first-year student in the Counseling Psychology doctoral program at UAlbany.
I earned my bachelor's degrees in psychology and family, youth and community sciences from the University of Florida, as well as my Master of Public Health (MPH). After graduating with my master's, I worked as a Public Health Fellow for the Florida Department of Health supporting HIV prevention efforts.
My research interests include identity development, minority stress and stigma, and suicide prevention among marginalized populations. In my free time, I enjoy cooking and trying new restaurants, birdwatching, reading, and spending time with loved ones.

Hello! My name is Ifeoma Akwue, I am a first-year doctoral student in the Counseling Psychology program. I am a Nigerian American from Florida. I graduated from the University of Florida with my B.S. in Psychology, emphasis in Behavioral and Cognitive Neuroscience.  I am interested in conducting culturally responsive, trauma-informed research for underserved populations. In my free time, I enjoy exploring public libraries, walking in nature, and playing Stardew Valley.

Joe is a first-year PhD student in the Counseling Psychology program at UAlbany. He grew up in Central, New York, nearby Syracuse. In 2024, he earned his bachelor's degree in psychology with a minor in Gender and Sexuality Studies at University at Buffalo. After graduating from UB, he worked as a research assistant at the Buffalo VA Medical Center. At VA, he assisted with clinical trials investigating the efficacy of biopsychosocial health interventions designed for primary care settings. His personal research interests center on LGBTQ+ behavioral health promotion, with a specific focus on alcohol misuse behavior among queer young adults. In his free time, he enjoys going thrift shopping, indoor gardening, and traveling.

Hi! I’m Aysha, a first-year Counseling Psychology PhD student at UAlbany and a part-time research coordinator studying trauma and resilience in healthcare workers. I hold a bachelor's in clinical psychology from CUNY Hunter College. My research focuses on trauma, mental health, and resilience in underserved and immigrant populations, specifically examining how social determinants of health and cultural values influence psychopathology. I am committed to advancing cultural competence within counseling psychology and aim to work in an academic medical center serving diverse communities. Outside of academia, I enjoy nature walks, traveling, and cooking.
